label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 9
knowledgePattern: Count valid SSA triangles including tangent and collapsed boundaries
solution:
The sine rule gives sinCt=sin45∘10, so sinC=t102. Thus no triangle is possible when t>102.

For 0<t<102, let the acute solution for C be α. The other possibility is 180∘−α. With A=45∘, the acute choice always leaves a positive angle at B. The obtuse choice leaves B=α−45∘, so it works only when α>45∘, equivalently t>10.

Therefore 0<t≤10 gives just one triangle, while 10<t<102 gives two. At t=10, the second choice has a zero angle and is excluded. At t=102, both angle choices become C=90∘, giving one triangle again.

Hence 0<t≤10 or t=102. Answer C.

hints.title: Use the sine rule for angle C
hints.body: Sketch the triangle. The side opposite angle A is 10, and the side opposite angle C is t. Write the sine rule to express sin C in terms of t.
hints.recap: Match each side with the angle opposite it.
hints.pitfall: The sine rule can give two possible angles.
hints.pause: Find the possible angles C for a given t.

recall.reminder: Match each side with the angle opposite it.

hints.title: Try both angles
hints.body: Call the acute angle with that sine value α. The other possible angle is 180∘−α. Test both with the given angle at A.
hints.recap: A triangle’s three angles add to 180 degrees.
hints.pitfall: The angle left for B must be strictly positive.
hints.pause: Decide when each possible angle C gives a valid triangle.

recall.reminder: A triangle’s three angles add to 180 degrees.

hints.title: Check where the cases meet
hints.body: Check the case where C is a right angle, so the two sine-rule angles coincide. Also check where one choice would leave angle B equal to zero.
hints.recap: At a boundary, two triangles can merge or one can collapse.
hints.pitfall: A collapsed triangle does not count.
hints.pause: Collect all t values that give exactly one triangle.
